categories.summary: No new attacks found today. This week Iran struck a US radar site in Bahrain (17 Nov), a US jet hit an Iranian missile site, a tanker was attacked in Hormuz, and Iran fired drones at a US base in Kuwait (18 Nov, shot down). The US is still sending more ships and troops. Taiwan, Korea and Russia-NATO show no new warning signs.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure

sources.title: DNI Clayton, FBI downplay cyberattacks amid major outages
NSA classified network, Apple services go down

categories.summary: A run of big US outages continues: Chase and other banks, Microsoft, Apple, a nationwide flight stop, and now a US spy agency (NSA) classified network. US intelligence and FBI chiefs say there is no evidence of a coordinated cyber attack; the known causes so far are faults. Separately, suspected Iran-linked hackers keep targeting supermarket fridges and small water systems in Europe and the US (France blames Iran; not officially confirmed as one campaign). The collector's 'China campaign' mixes in the Microsoft bug and a criminal gang's Visa claim, so that link looks weak. Nothing reported in Australia; our banks, phones and grid are normal.

headline: No new Gulf attacks today, but the Strait of Hormuz stays shut and the US-Iran standoff keeps fuel dear.
summary: A quiet day: no new attacks on US bases or tankers were reported after this week's exchanges in Bahrain, Kuwait and Hormuz, and oil eased a little. The run of big US outages (banks, Microsoft, Apple, flights, a spy agency network) goes on, but US officials say there is no sign of a cyber attack behind them, and nothing has hit Australia. Storms cut power to over 20,000 homes on Eyre Peninsula, far from us. Fire danger in the Hills drops to Moderate tomorrow.
